title: I built a cargo ship puzzle game with Claude Opus 5.5 as my coding partner: load the hold, keep her level, sail to 120 real ports
author: RepairVisual136
selftext:
Hi everyone! I'm a solo developer and I just released my first puzzle game on Google Play: Cargo Trim.

The idea is simple: you load crates into a ship's hold, but the ship has to float level. Too much weight at the bow and she dives, too much at the stern and she tips back. A trim meter at the top shows you where the needle is, and if you get it into the green you set sail. Get it perfect and you earn 3 stars.

What's in it:

• Hundreds of levels on a voyage through 120 real ports across Europe and Africa

• A real map you sail across, with a passport that collects stamps from every port

• Your own harbour to build up and a ship you can paint

• Regional music that changes as you sail to new places

• Short levels, no timers, good for a coffee break

How it was made: I built it in Godot 4, and I made the whole thing together with Claude Opus 5.5. It worked as my coding partner, helped with the physics of the trim, the level design, the map, the store listing and the trailers. I'm a one-person studio, so having an AI partner let me ship something much bigger than I could have alone. Every design decision and every test on real phones was still mine.

It's free (ads only, no pay-to-win).

Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=hr.maximize.cargotrim&referrer=utm\_source%3Dreddit%26utm\_medium%3Dsocial

I'd really love honest feedback, especially on difficulty: are the early levels too easy or too hard? Thanks for reading! 🚢
